To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed an EGS which targets the NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor, and we have demonstrated the potency of the molecule to reduce NR1 mRNA levels in neurons.

the expression of a small RNA molecule in neurons can lead to the specific cleavage of the mRNA for the NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor and that this reduction in NR1 subunit expression is neuroprotective.
a small RNA molecule that targets a specific mRNA for RNase‐P‐dependent cleavage can be used to reduce the abundance of a specific protein in neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies to reduce the expression level of a specific gene in neurons.

the development of a strategy to reduce the functional expression of a specific NMDA receptor protein subunit within neurons and to determine the role of this subunit in synaptic plasticity and neuronal survival.
the development of a novel strategy to reduce the expression and function of the NR1 subunit of NMDA receptors in cortical neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the EGSs in neurons is a novel approach to reduce the expression and function of any gene in neurons.
the use of the EGS approach to reduce NR1 expression is a promising strategy to study the function of NMDA receptors.
the use of an EGS directed against the NR1 mRNA can reduce the amount of the protein in neurons, and that the reduction of NR1 protein is neuroprotective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel strategy for the reduction of a specific gene in neurons, which has been demonstrated to be neuroprotective.

we have developed a novel approach to reduce the expression and function of a specific NMDA receptor protein subunit in vivo and that the reduction in NR1 protein expression is associated with neuroprotection.
we have demonstrated the ability to selectively reduce the expression of a specific gene (NR1) in neurons and that this reduction is sufficient to provide a functional benefit in an in vivo system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reduction of NR1 expression in neurons is neuroprotecting, and that the reduction of functional NR1 expression in the CNS could be a viable therapeutic strategy for the treatment of excitotoxicity‐related disorders.

we have shown that it is feasible to use EGSs in vivo to achieve the goal of reducing the expression of a specific protein in neurons and this approach should have wide applicability to the study of the functional role of specific genes in the brain.
EGS‐mediated mRNA cleavage represents a new and powerful approach to reducing the expression of a specific protein in neurons.
